'''Raymond James Carroll''' is an American [[statistician]], and [[Distinguished Professor]] of [[statistics]], [[nutrition]] and [[toxicology]] at [[Texas A&M University]]. He is a recipient of 1988 [[COPSS Presidents' Award]] and 2002 [[R. A. Fisher Lectureship]]. He has made fundamental contributions to [[measurement error model]], [[nonparametric regression|nonparametric]] and [[semiparametric regression|semiparametric modeling]].

==Biography==
Carroll was born in Japan of military parents in 1949 and grew up in [[Washington, D.C.]], Germany and [[Wichita Falls, Texas]]. He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 1971 and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[statistics]] from [[Purdue University]] in 1974 under the supervision of [[Shanti S. Gupta]].<ref name="Shanti S. Gupta" /> He was on the faculty at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] from 1974 to 1987. He also had visiting positions at the [[University of Heidelberg]], the [[University of Wisconsin]], and the [[National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute]]. Carroll has been a [[full professor]] of statistics,<ref name="RJC's departmental directory" /> nutrition<ref name="Nutrition faculty list" /> and toxicology<ref name="Toxicology faculty list" /> at [[Texas A&M University]] since 1987, was head of the Department of Statistics from 1987 to 1990,<ref name="Strength in Numbers"/> and was named a [[Distinguished Professor]]<ref name="TAMU Science DP" /><ref name="TAMU DP list" /> in 1997. He has visiting appointments at the [[Australian National University]], the [[Humboldt University]] in [[Berlin]] and the [[National Cancer Institute]]. He was the founding director of the Texas A&M Center for Statistical [[Bioinformatics]],<ref name="Center for Statistical Bioinformatics" /> and has been the director of Texas A&M Institute for [[Applied mathematics|Applied Mathematics]] and [[Computational science|Computational Science]] since 2010.<ref name="RJC IAMCS" /> He holds an [[honorary doctorate]] from the Institut de Statistique, [[Université Catholique de Louvain]] in [[Belgium]].<ref name="honorary doctorate uclouvain" /><ref name="honorary doctorate uclouvain tamu" />

Carroll's many areas of research include [[measurement error model]], [[nonparametric regression|nonparametric]] and [[semiparametric regression]], [[inverse problem]], [[functional data analysis]], [[case-control studies]], among others. His work has a broad variety of application fields, including radiation and [[nutritional epidemiology]], [[molecular biology]], [[genomics]] and many others. He has authored or coauthored four books,<ref name="RJC books" /> over 300 refereed papers and has given over 300 invited talks. He has supervised and mentored more than 30 [[Ph.D.]] students<ref name="RJC students" /> and can claim more than 90 descendants in his [[Mathematics Genealogy Project|mathematical genealogy]].<ref name="RJC Mathematics Genealogy" />

He received the [[COPSS Presidents' Award]]<ref name="RJC Presidents' Award" /> in 1988 and gave the [[R. A. Fisher Lectureship|Fisher Lecture]]<ref name="RJC Fisher" /> at the 2002 [[Joint Statistical Meetings]]. He was the first [[statistician]] given a Method to Extend Research in Time (MERIT) Award from the [[National Cancer Institute]].<ref name="RJC MERIT Award" /> He served as editor of [[Biometrics (journal)|Biometrics]]<ref name="Biometrics Vol. 53, No. 4"/> and [[Journal of the American Statistical Association]] (Theory and Methods),<ref name="RJC JASA editor 1989" /><ref name="RJC JASA editor 1990" /> and chair of [[American Statistical Association|ASA]]'s Section on Nonparametric Statistics.<ref name="RJC NP Chair" /> A conference on "Statistical Methods for Complex Data" was held on the [[Texas A&M University campus]] in honor of Carroll in 2009.<ref name="RJC conference 2009" /> In the same year, the Raymond J. Carroll Young Investigator Award was established to honor Carroll for his fundamental contributions in many areas of statistical methodology and practice.<ref name="RJC Young Investigator Award" /> The award is given bi-annually on odd numbered years to a statistician who has made important contributions to the area of statistics, with the recipients being [[Samuel Kou]] and [[Marc A. Suchard]], both are also [[COPSS Presidents' Award]] recipients.<ref name="RJC Young Investigator Award Kou" /> Ray Carroll was in the selection committee of COPSS Presidents' Award during that period.

==Personal life==
Carroll is married to Texas A&M behavioral scientist [[Marcia G. Ory]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hutchins |first1=Shana K. |title=Texas A&M Faculty Couple Funds Fellowship for Graduate Students in Statistics |url=https://science.tamu.edu/news/2015/10/texas-am-faculty-couple-funds-fellowship-for-graduate-students-in-statistics/ |website=tamus.edu |access-date=May 30, 2021 |date=October 27, 2015}}</ref>

* 2013 Fellow, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref name="AAAS 2013 Fellows" /><ref name="AAAS 2013 Fellows College of Science Announcement" />
* 2012 [[Honorary Doctorate]], Institut de Statistique, [[Université Catholique de Louvain]]<ref name="honorary doctorate uclouvain" /><ref name="honorary doctorate uclouvain tamu" />
* 2005 MERIT Award, [[National Cancer Institute]]<ref name="RJC MERIT Award" />
* 2003 [[Mitchell Prize]], [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]]<ref name="RJC Mitchell Prize" /><ref name="JASA 2003" />
* 2003 [[Journal of the American Statistical Association|JASA]] Applications Editor Invited Paper<ref name="JASA 2003" />
* 2003 [[Jerome Sacks Award for Outstanding Cross-Disciplinary Research]], [[National Institute of Statistical Sciences]]<ref name="Sacks Award 2003" /><ref name="Sacks Award" />
* 2002 [[R. A. Fisher Lectureship]], [[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies]]<ref name="RJC Fisher" />
* 1997 [[Snedecor Award]], [[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies|COPSS]]<ref name="RJC Snedecor Award" /><ref name="JASA 1996" />
* 1994 Distinguished Alumnus, College of Science, [[Purdue University]]<ref name="RJC Distinguished Alumnus" />
* 1994 Don Owen Award, [[American Statistical Association|ASA]]'s San Antonio Chapter<ref name="RJC Don Owen Award" />
* 1988 [[COPSS Presidents' Award]]<ref name="RJC Presidents' Award" />
* 1984 Fellow, [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]<ref name="RJC IMS Fellow" />
* 1982 Fellow, [[American Statistical Association]]<ref name="RJC ASA Fellow" />
